THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT PRAYING TO SET ASIDE THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 02.11.2018 PASSED BY II ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE & ADDITIONAL MACT-8, SHIVAMOGGA IN MVC NO.395/2016 AWARDING COMPENSATION OF RS.12,80,000/- WITH INTEREST AT 6% P.A., FROM THE DATE OF THE ORDER TILL THE DATE OF DEPOSIT.

THESE MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEALS COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING THIS DAY, K.S.MUDAGAL J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Challenging the award in M.V.C.No.395/2016 on the file of II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT-8, NC: 2023:KHC:25366-DB Shivamogga, the claimant has preferred M.F.A.No.8633/2019 and the Insurer has preferred M.F.A.No.1160/2019.
Shri Nagrajappa vs Smt.Neelamma on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111870012/
3
2. The appellant in M.F.A.No.8633/2019 is the claimant.
Respondent Nos.1 to 3 in the said appeal were the respondents in M.V.C.No.395/2016.
For the purpose of convenience, the parties will be referred to henceforth according to their ranks before the Tribunal.
3. The claim petition was filed by the next friend who is the wife of the claimant.
On 24.07.2015 at 7.30 p.m. the claimant met with accident near Yalavalli bridge, Aynuru Village within the limits of Kumsi police station.

Regarding the accident, on 25.07.2015 at 12.30 p.m. i.e. on next day, the complaint as per Ex.P3 was filed by PW.2 Lokeshappa before Kumsi police alleging that, on that day himself and Veerashappa his villager were proceeding on motorbike bearing Registration No.KA-14- ED-9752.

He further alleged that near Yalavalli bridge, respondent No.2 rode the said motorbike in rash and negligent manner and hit the claimant who was pedestrian, consequently the claimant and PW.2 both suffered grievous injuries.
Respondent No.2 had not suffered any injury.
Then himself and NC: 2023:KHC:25366-DB the claimant were shifted to Ayanuru Hospital.
From there, himself and the claimant were shifted to McGann Hospital.
4. Based on the said complaint, the first information report as per Ex.P2 in Crime No.165/2015 of Kumsi police station was registered.
On investigation, the police filed charge sheet as per Ex.P8 against respondent No.2.
Ex . P63

the certified copy of the order sheet in C.C.No.1101/2016 on the file of the Principal Civil Judge (Junior Division) & J.M.F.C. Shivamogga arising out of Crime No.165/2015 shows that on 17.03.2017 respondent No.2 pleaded guilty.
He was convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 and 338 of IPC and sentenced to fine.
At the time of the accident, respondent Nos.1 and 3 were the registered owner and insurer of the motorbike No.KA-14-ED-9752.

Respondent No.1 is none else the mother of respondent No.2.
5.

The claimant filed M.V.C.No.395/2016 alleging that when he was walking on the road near Yalavalli bridge, respondent No.2 by riding the motorbike bearing No.KA-14-ED-9752 in rash and negligent manner hit him and caused him grievous injuries.
He further alleged that he suffered grievous injuries in the accident, consequently 100% permanent physical disability.

He claimed that at the time of the accident, NC: 2023:KHC:25366-DB he was aged 48 years, earning Rs.25,000/-
per month by doing agricultural work.
Due to the accidental injuries, he has lost his future earnings.
He claimed compensation of Rs.42,80,000/- on different heads.

6. Respondent Nos.1 to 3 contested the petition denying the involvement of motorbike bearing No.KA-14-ED-9752 in the alleged accident, actionable negligence on the part of respondent No.2,
age, occupation, income of the claimant, permanent physical disability suffered by him and its liability to pay the compensation.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 contended that respondent No.2 was having valid driving licence and the vehicle was insured with respondent No.3.
Therefore even if any compensation has to be awarded, respondent No.3 is liable to pay the same.
7. To substantiate his contention, on behalf of the claimant, his next friend was examined as PW.1.
The complainant/alleged eyewitness was examined as PW.2 and the doctor who treated the claimant was examined as PW.3.
On behalf of the claimant, Ex.P1 to P63 were marked.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 did not lead any evidence nor they cross-
examined the claimant's witnesses.
Respondent No.3 examined its Official as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R1 to R3.

Shri Nagrajappa vs Smt.Neelamma on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111870012/
4 NC: 2023:KHC:25366-DB 8.

The Tribunal on hearing the parties by the impugned award relying on the evidence of PW.2, the police records namely Exs.P1 to P6 the police notice, the first information report, statement, spot mahazar, sketch of scene of offence, IMV report, Ex.P8 the charge sheet and Ex.P63 the copy of the order sheet in C.C.No.1101/2016 where under respondent No.2 was convicted and sentenced based on plea of guilt, held that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of respondent No.2 in the manner alleged.

The Tribunal relying on medical records, considered the age of the claimant as 51 to 55 years, relying on the evidence of PW.3 and the medical records, assessed his disability at 75% to the whole body and his income notionally at Rs.9,000/- per month, applied 11 multiplier and awarded Rs.8,91,000/- on the head of loss of future earnings.

The Tribunal in all awarded compensation of Rs.12,80,537/- on different heads as per the table below:
 Sl. Particulars Compensation  No. amount  1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs.1,00,000/-
 2. Towards loss of future income Rs.8,91,000/-

3 . Towards medical expenses Rs.2,49,537/-
 4. Towards conveyance, attendant Rs.40,000/-
 charges, food and nourishment  Total Rs.12,80,537/-
 NC: 2023:KHC:25366-DB  9.
The claimant has challenged the said award questioning the adequacy of the compensation awarded to him.
The Insurer has challenged the award disputing both involvement of the insured vehicle in the accident and the quantum of compensation.

Submissions of Smt.Lakshmi, learned Counsel for the claimant:
10. PW.2 is the eyewitness and person injured in the accident.
On his complaint against respondent No.2 and on investigation, the police filed charge sheet against respondent No.2.
He pleaded guilty and was convicted and sentenced.
The said evidence was sufficient to hold that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of respondent No.2 involving the insured motorbike.
The respondents were not able to rebut such evidence.
Therefore the Tribunal was justified in holding that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of respondent No.2 in driving the motorbike bearing No.KA-14-ED-9752.
So far as the compensation, Ex.P12 ration card had come into existence prior to the accident where age of the claimant was shown as 48 years.
That was issued by the Government Authority.
That takes precedence.

The Tribunal assessing the age of the claimant Shri Nagrajappa vs Smt.Neelamma on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111870012/
5 between 51 to 55 years NC: 2023:KHC:25366-DB overlooking Ex.P12 is erroneous.
Exs.P55 and P56 show that the claimant had wet cultivable land.

Therefore the Tribunal committed error in assessing his income notionally at Rs.9,000/-
per month.
The assessment of permanent physical disability at 75% is contrary to the evidence of the doctor.
The compensation awarded on all other heads is also on the lower side.
The Tribunal ought to have awarded compensation towards loss of amenities, attendant charges to the claimant for his whole life, loss of income during laid up period.
Before this Court, the claimant's Counsel files memo of calculation of compensation quantifying the compensation at Rs.62,69,537/-.
Thus she seeks enhancement of the compensation.

Submissions of Sri B.Pradeep, learned Counsel for respondent No.3-Insurer:
11.
The evidence of PWs.1 and 2 shows that the claimant, PW.2 and respondent No.2 are closely related to each other.

The evidence on record shows that at the time of accident, the claimant himself was riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and there was skid of the motorbike.
Due to the said impact, the claimant and PW.2 both sustained injuries.
Ex . R3

wound certificate of PW.2 and Exs.P9 and P10, the discharge summary relating to the claimant show that at the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:25366-DB earliest point of time, they reported in the hospital with a history of skid and fall while the claimant himself riding the motorcycle.

However, later respondent No.2, PW.2,
the claimant in collusion with the Police, Transport authorities and others to make wrongful gain filed complaint and implicated the insured vehicle.

The charge sheet or plea of guilt are not the conclusive proof of the involvement of the insured vehicle, the Court has to examine the other independent evidence produced before it in an integrated manner.

There are unambiguous admissions on the part of PWs.1 and 2 regarding the age of the claimant, the relationship of PWs.1, 2 and respondent No.2, the manner of occurrence of the accident, the Tribunal has failed to examine the evidence in a judicious manner which has lead to miscarriage of justice.
Thus he sought for dismissal of the petition.

12. On hearing both side and on examination of the records, the questions that arise for consideration of this Court are:
(i) Whether the finding of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence of respondent No.2 in - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:25366-DB riding motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-14-ED-9752 is sustainable in law?

Shri Nagrajappa vs Smt.Neelamma on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111870012/
6 (ii) Whether the compensation awarded is just one?
Analysis Reg. Point No.1:
13.

When the claimant came before the Court alleging that on 24.07.2015 at 7.30 p.m. when he was walking near Yalavalli bridge, respondent No.2 riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-14-ED-9752 in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life, hit him, caused the accident leading to grievous injuries, the burden of proving the said facts is on him.

To prove the said facts, the claimant relied on the evidence of PWs.1 and 2 and Ex.P1 to P6, the police notice, the first information report,
statement, spot Mahazar, sketch, IMV report, Ex.P8 the charge sheet and Ex.P63 the copy of the order sheet in C.C.No.1101/2016.
14.
According to the learned counsel for the claimant, the said evidence conclusively prove the involvement of the motorcycle and actionable negligence on the part of respondent No.2.

Whether the charge sheet and plea of guilt of the alleged driver of the vehicle are the conclusive proof of the occurrence - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:25366-DB of the accident or involvement of the vehicle as alleged was dealt with by this Court in the following cases:
1. Veerappa v.Siddappa1 2. Mahadevi and others vs. Shivaputra & others2 3. Bajaj Allianz vs. B.C.Kumar3 .
15. Taking note of disturbing trend of unscrupulous persons filing claim petitions falsely implicating insured vehicle in collusion with Police, Doctors and even the Insurance Company to make wrongful gain, the coordinate Bench of this Court in para 16 of the judgment in Veerappa's case referred to supra held as follows:

entities.text: Mahadevi and others vs. Shivaputra & others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Sub Section(2) of Section 149 provides the grounds on which the insurance company can avoid the liability to pay the compensation under the Act.
One such ground is, if a policy is obtained by a representation of fact which was false in some material particular.

Section 172 confers on the Claims Tribunal a power to award compensatory costs, if it is satisfied that the policy of insurance is void on the ground that it was obtained by representation of fact which was false in any material particular or any party or insured has put forward a false or vexatious claim or defence.
Sub-Section (3) of Section 172 also speaks of criminal liability in respect of such misrepresentation.

ILR 2009 KAR 3562 MFA No.201689/2016 DD 20.11.2020 ILR 2009 KAR 2921 - 13 - Shri Nagrajappa vs Smt.Neelamma on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111870012/
7 NC: 2023:KHC:25366-DB
However, it restricts the compensatory costs to be awarded to only Rs.1,000/- .
Therefore, the Act provides for taking action against a party who sets up a false or vexatious defence.
However, the cost of Rs. 1,000/- prescribed under the aforesaid provision, has failed to act as a sufficient deterrent to the parties setting up false claim or defence.
The experience has shown that this branch of law is slowly getting into the hands of unscrupulous people who are making a mockery of judicial process.

A disturbing trend of unholy alliance among the police, the doctors, the lawyers and some times even the Insurance Company, to siphon out the public money,
and make an unlawful gain is fast emerging.
It is also gaining respectability and persons who indulge in such practices are acclaimed as most successful in their respective profession.
This is a dangerous trend, if unchecked would undermine the judicial process.
As the existing law is inadequate to check this malady, the Courts not only have to be careful in adjudicating such claims but also find ways to prevent such abuse.

They have to balance the interest of these accident victims and their legal heirs on one side, by giving them just compensation at the earliest, thus giving effect to the mandate of the parliament, and on the other hand, to see that the very process is not abused and exploited by a handful of persons, who have attained specialization in this field, to make personal gains at the cost of the exchequer.
An onerous responsibility lies on the Courts.

Therefore,
it is imperative that a strong message is to be sent to the abusers of the judicial process to discourage them from indulging in such practices as well as the consequences of such - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:25366-DB abuse may result in foisting the liability exclusively on the insured owner of the vehicle".
(Emphasis supplied)
16. It was further held having regard to the said trend, the Courts have to take into consideration the charge sheet in criminal proceedings and evaluate that along with other evidence on record.
The same view was taken in by this Court in Mahadevi's case referred to supra.

In B.C.Kumar's case referred to supra, it was held that even if the alleged driver of the vehicle pleads guilty that is not the conclusive proof and that has to be evaluated with reference to other evidence on record.

Therefore,
it is clear that the charge sheet or the alleged rider pleading guilty are not conclusive proof and the Court has to evaluate the entire evidence on record in an integrated manner.
17. In this case, PW.1 was not an eyewitness.
PW.2 the complainant who filed complaint against respondent No.2 though claims that he and others shifted the injured-claimant to hospital, there is one day delay in filing the complaint.
PWs.1 and 2 both admit in their cross-examination that themselves and respondent No.2 are related to each other.
Despite that in the complaint-Ex.P3, he does not divulge his relationship with - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:25366-DB the claimant or respondent No.2.
He gives the complaint as if he was a stranger to the claimant.

Shri Nagrajappa vs Smt.Neelamma on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111870012/
8 18.
According to PW.2, respondent No.2 was riding the motorcycle.
In the accident, himself and respondent No.2 suffered injuries.
They were taken to the hospital.
He admits that he gave the history of the accident before the Doctor.
He further admits that bike on which he was traveling had no insurance.
That substantiates the contention of the learned Counsel for respondent No.3 that vehicle involved in the accident was some other uninsured vehicle.
Further Ex.R3 the wound certificate issued by Mc.Gann Hospital, Shivamogga relating to PW.2 shows that PW.2 reported in the said hospital on 24.07.2015 at 7.30 p.m.

The history given before the Doctor as per Ex.R3 is as follows:
"History of RTA bike hit to bullock cart at 7.30 p.m. on 24.7.2015 at Ayanur"
19.
Though PW.2 says respondent No.2 also suffered injuries, the charge sheet does not mention any injury suffered by respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2 did not get himself examined to deny the allegations of implication of the vehicle falsely.
Exs. P9
and P10 are the claimants own documents.
Ex . P9

discharge summary issued by Nanjappa Hospital, Shivamogga,
- 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:25366-DB Ex.P10 is styled as Clinical discharge summary issued by NH Sahyadri Narayana Multispeciality Hospital, Shivamogga.

entities.text: NH Sahyadri Narayana Multispeciality Hospital, Shivamogga
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Ex.P9 states that the claimant was admitted into the said hospital on 24.07.2015 at 9.43 p.m. and the history mentioned in the said document is as follows:
"Alleged history of RTA - skid and fall from Bike near Elavalli bridge, near Ayanur at around 7.30 p.m. on 24.07.2015"
Ex.P10 shows that the claimant was admitted in the said hospital on 25.07.2015 and discharged on 22.08.2015.

The history given in both hospitals are:
"Alleged history of RTA skid and fall near Elavalli Bridge, near Ayanur at around 7.30 a.m. on 24.7.2015 and sustained injury to head"
20.
Ex . P9
states that patient was unconscious.

Since the history given in Exs.P9 and P10 and Ex.R3 at the earliest point of time that too by the attendants of the claimant/injured themselves that carries more credibility whereas, the complaint was filed after one day.
Ex.P2 shows FIR was delivered to the Court on 25.07.2015 at 4.40 p.m.

That clearly shows that there was scope for deliberations and on such deliberations, insured vehicle and the theory of respondent No.2 being the rider of the motorcycle and the claimant being pedestrian are introduced.
Thereby the defence of respondent No.3 stood - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:25366-DB probabilized.
That gets further substantiated by the fact of relationship of PW.2, respondent No.2 and the claimant.

Though PW.2 says that respondent No.2 had also suffered Shri Nagrajappa vs Smt.Neelamma on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111870012/
9 injuries, the same does not reflect in the charge sheet.

21. The Tribunal without appreciating the aforesaid circumstances and weighing Exs.P9, P10 and Ex.R3 as against the police records, the admissions of PW.2 and the ratio of the aforesaid judgments of this Court, hurriedly concluded that the charge sheet and other police records are the conclusive proof and such evidence was not rebutted.
Therefore, the said finding with regard to involvement of insured vehicle and negligence on the part of respondent No.2 is unsustainable.
Therefore, the claim petition is liable to be dismissed.

Reg. Point No.2:
22.
In view of finding on point No.1, this point does not survive for further consideration.
23. For the aforesaid reasons, the insurer's appeal succeeds and the appeal of the claimant is liable to be dismissed.

Hence, the following:
ORDER MFA No.8633/2019 is hereby dismissed.
is hereby allowed with costs.
The impugned judgment and award is hereby set aside.
The claim petition filed by the claimant in M.V.C.No.395/2016 on the file of II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT- 8, Shivamogga is hereby dismissed with costs.
Registry shall refund the amount in deposit, if any, to the appellant in MFA No.1160/2019 digitally and return the trial Court records to the Tribunal.

opennyai_summary.facts:
He was convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 and 338 of IPC and sentenced to fine.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 contended that respondent No.2 was having valid driving licence and the vehicle was insured with respondent No.3.
The Tribunal relying on medical records, considered the age of the claimant as 51 to 55 years, relying on the evidence of PW.3 and the medical records, assessed his disability at 75% to the whole body and his income notionally at Rs.9,000/- per month, applied 11 multiplier and awarded Rs.8,91,000/- on the head of loss of future earnings.
The Tribunal in all awarded compensation of Rs.12,80,537/- on different heads as per the table below:
 Sl. Particulars Compensation  No. amount  1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs.1,00,000/-
 2. Towards loss of future income Rs.8,91,000/-
The claimant has challenged the said award questioning the adequacy of the compensation awarded to him.
The Insurer has challenged the award disputing both involvement of the insured vehicle in the accident and the quantum of compensation.
On his complaint against respondent No.2 and on investigation, the police filed charge sheet against respondent No.2.
He pleaded guilty and was convicted and sentenced.
The said evidence was sufficient to hold that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of respondent No.2 involving the insured motorbike.
The respondents were not able to rebut such evidence.
Therefore the Tribunal was justified in holding that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of respondent No.2 in driving the motorbike bearing No.KA-14-ED-9752.
So far as the compensation, Ex.P12 ration card had come into existence prior to the accident where age of the claimant was shown as 48 years.
Therefore the Tribunal committed error in assessing his income notionally at Rs.9,000/-
per month.
The assessment of permanent physical disability at 75% is contrary to the evidence of the doctor.
The Tribunal ought to have awarded compensation towards loss of amenities, attendant charges to the claimant for his whole life, loss of income during laid up period.
There are unambiguous admissions on the part of PWs.1 and 2 regarding the age of the claimant, the relationship of PWs.1, 2 and respondent No.2, the manner of occurrence of the accident, the Tribunal has failed to examine the evidence in a judicious manner which has lead to miscarriage of justice.
When the claimant came before the Court alleging that on 24.07.2015 at 7.30 p.m. when he was walking near Yalavalli bridge, respondent No.2 riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-14-ED-9752 in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life, hit him, caused the accident leading to grievous injuries, the burden of proving the said facts is on him.

Section 172 confers on the Claims Tribunal a power to award compensatory costs, if it is satisfied that the policy of insurance is void on the ground that it was obtained by representation of fact which was false in any material particular or any party or insured has put forward a false or vexatious claim or defence.
ILR 2009 KAR 3562 MFA No.201689/2016 DD 20.11.2020 ILR 2009 KAR 2921 - 13 - Shri Nagrajappa vs Smt.Neelamma on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111870012/

The experience has shown that this branch of law is slowly getting into the hands of unscrupulous people who are making a mockery of judicial process.
It is also gaining respectability and persons who indulge in such practices are acclaimed as most successful in their respective profession.
As the existing law is inadequate to check this malady, the Courts not only have to be careful in adjudicating such claims but also find ways to prevent such abuse.
They have to balance the interest of these accident victims and their legal heirs on one side, by giving them just compensation at the earliest, thus giving effect to the mandate of the parliament, and on the other hand, to see that the very process is not abused and exploited by a handful of persons, who have attained specialization in this field, to make personal gains at the cost of the exchequer.
